why: Telemetry for the crash-loop case, and the corpus's first series that needs a window longer than half an hour: the text's own count is 178 restarts in twelve hours, so the window is twelve hours and the samples spread across it. This is only expressible because the cadence follows the window -- with eight samples ninety seconds apart, declaring 178 would have compressed twelve hours into twelve minutes. The counter is the honest shape here: it accumulates from zero, and its last sample is exactly the declared 178 at the window's end. The probe ratio is the second half of the mechanism and it is flat at zero, which is what 'no probe ever passes' says; a flat zero is also the control that separates this from a container that starts and then fails its probe.

series.why: the checkpoint `cp-restarts` holds the text's count, and the counter accumulates to it by the end of the twelve-hour window

series.quote: before the HTTP listener comes up, so no probe ever passes
series.why: the checkpoint `cp-probe` holds the zero: the process exits before the listener can answer a probe, which is why the probe is not the cause; probe outcomes are counted, so a run where no probe passed reads exactly zero

logs.body: SIGSEGV in native ffmpeg binding 1.8s after accepting job 0x41f2, listener not yet bound
logs.quote: logs a segmentation fault in the native ffmpeg binding within two seconds of receiving the first job
logs.why: the crash itself, on every start, which is the sentence the log checkpoint quotes
